issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary cannot obtain specific performance of a conditional right to reconveyance when a condition of that right has not been strictly fulfilled, absent an equitable exception.
material_facts: The owner conveyed the property by a sale deed and received a separate deed granting a right to reconveyance, subject to payment within two years and a condition that rent not remain in arrears for more than six months.
The rent fell into arrears for seven months, so the rent condition was not fulfilled, although the right was exercised within the specified period.
The owner sought specific performance and argued that equity should relieve against the loss of the reconveyance right.
issues.conclusion: The right to demand reconveyance could not be enforced because the rent condition was not fulfilled, and the court had no equitable jurisdiction to relieve against its extinction. The decree granting specific performance was set aside and the trial court’s dismissal of the suit restored.
issues.legal_principle: A reconveyance option reserved for the original owner is a concession or privilege exercisable only on strict fulfilment of its conditions. Although equity may relieve against penalties intended to secure payment or performance where the failure can be compensated, that principle does not apply to a beneficial right that arises only upon performance in a stated manner or at a stated time; absent fraud, accident, or surprise, equity will not relieve against breach of those terms. The Court followed the majority in Shanmugam Pillai v. Annalakshmi Ammal (A.I.R. 1950 F.C. 38), and referred to John H. Kilmer v. British Columbia Orchard Lands Ltd. (L.R. (1913) A.C. 319), Devendra Prasad Sukul v. Surendra Prasad Sukul (L.R. 63 I.A. 26), and Davis v. Thomas (39 E.R. 195).

predicates.specific_performance_claim_for_reconveya: A claimant seeks specific performance of a right to have property reconveyed.
predicates.reconveyance_right_is_a_conditional_conc: The right to reconveyance was granted as a concession subject to stated conditions.
predicates.a_reconveyance_condition_was_not_fulfill: The claimant failed to fulfil at least one condition required to exercise the reconveyance right.
predicates.equitable_exception_event_exists: Fraud, accident, or surprise affected the failure to fulfil the condition.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance of a conditional reconveyance concession, has failed to fulfil a condition, and no equitable exception event exists, specific performance is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A sale cannot be treated as a mortgage by conditional sale when the sale and the condition for repurchase are set out in separate documents.
material_facts: The property was conveyed by a sale deed, while the covenant granting the right to reconveyance was contained in a separate document.
The claimant sought to establish that the transaction was in the nature of a mortgage by conditional sale.
issues.conclusion: The claim that the transaction was a mortgage by conditional sale was inadmissible because the sale deed and the covenant for reconveyance were in separate documents.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 58(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, as applied by the Court, a sale and the condition for repurchase must be contained in the same document for the transaction to be treated as a mortgage by conditional sale; separate documents do not permit proof of that characterization.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding_involves: A proceeding seeking specific performance of reconveyance also involves a claim that the sale was a mortgage by conditional sale.
predicates.claimant_seeks_to_characterize_sale_as_c: The claimant seeks to establish that the transaction was a mortgage by conditional sale.
predicates.sale_and_repurchase_condition_are_in_sep: The sale and the condition for repurchase were recorded in separate documents.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance proceeding involving a claim that a sale was a mortgage by conditional sale, that characterization claim is inadmissible if the sale and repurchase condition are in separate documents.
